headline: Progress Software told ShareFile customers to power down their servers over a credible threat, leading a day thick with actively exploited web flaws and ransomware guilty pleas.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep turning autonomous AI coding tools against their owners, hiding prompt injections in PNG images with a technique called Ghostcommit that walks code agents into leaking a repository's secrets.
A run of U.S. prosecutions—a Ryuk operator's guilty plea and a 70-month sentence for a BlackCat negotiator—shows law enforcement squeezing the people behind ransomware, not just their infrastructure.

Emergency directives are multiplying as Progress told ShareFile customers to power down Storage Zone Controllers over a credible threat, one of several urgent, actively exploited web-facing flaws surfacing in a single day.

topics.title: Actively Exploited Web-Facing Flaws
topics.latest_developments: CISA added two actively exploited file-upload flaws—CVE-2026-48939 in the iCagenda Joomla extension and CVE-2026-56291 in Balbooa Forms—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog July 10, the same day attackers began exploiting a critical Gitea Docker-image authentication bypass that lets them impersonate any user including administrators, as Zimbra urged customers to patch a critical Classic Web Client stored cross-site-scripting flaw that crafted emails abuse to run code in a user's session.
topics.summary: The flaws hit self-hosted Git services, Joomla sites, and the Zimbra collaboration suite, all internet-facing. Administrators should patch immediately and check for signs of compromise.

sources.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
Hackers exploit critical auth bypass in Gitea Docker image
Zimbra urges customers to patch critical web client XSS flaw
Critical Zimbra Flaw Could Let Crafted Emails Run Malicious Code in User Sessions

topics.title: Prompt Injection Against AI Agents
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer detailed July 11 "Ghostcommit," a technique that hides prompt injections inside PNG images and slips past AI code reviewers CodeRabbit and Bugbot—which never open image files—then tricks a coding agent into reading a repository's .env file and writing every secret into code as a list of numbers, as researchers disclosed three patched flaws in the OpenClaw personal AI assistant enabling credential theft, privilege escalation, and code execution on the host.
topics.summary: Prompt-injection attacks turn autonomous AI coding tools and assistants against their owners to steal credentials and repository secrets. Organizations should restrict agent access to files, secrets, and hosts.

sources.title: 'Ghostcommit' hides prompt injection in images to fool AI agents, steal secrets
Researcher Details WhatsApp-to-Host Attack Chain Using Three OpenClaw Flaws

topics.title: Ransomware Operators Face Prison
topics.latest_developments: In U.S. courts July 10 a 34-year-old Armenian man pleaded guilty in Oregon federal court to conspiracy and computer fraud for deploying Ryuk ransomware against American companies, facing up to 15 years, while a Florida court sentenced former ransomware negotiator Angelo Martino to 70 months for helping the BlackCat/AlphV gang extort victims, and Canada separately disrupted ransomware operations.
topics.summary: Ryuk and BlackCat/AlphV rank among the most prolific ransomware operations of recent years. The prosecutions extend sustained law-enforcement pressure aimed at operators and their enablers rather than only their servers.

sources.title: Ryuk ransomware member pleads guilty in the US, faces 15 years in prison
Ryuk operator pleads guilty; Blackcat/AlphV conspirator gets nearly 6-year sentence
Third US Security Expert Sentenced to Prison for Helping Ransomware Gang
In Other News: DHS Database Hacked, Adobe Boosts Patch Cadence, Canada Disrupts Ransomware Ops

topics.title: Progress ShareFile Emergency Shutdown
topics.latest_developments: Progress Software emailed ShareFile customers July 10, telling those who run Storage Zone Controllers on Windows servers to shut them down immediately over a confirmed "credible external security threat," and temporarily disabled access to affected accounts out of caution while it investigates.
topics.summary: ShareFile is Progress's enterprise secure file-sharing product, and Storage Zone Controllers manage its on-premises data storage. Administrators running the affected on-premises servers should power them down and await Progress guidance.

sources.title: URGENT - Progress Tells ShareFile Customers to Shut Down Storage Zone Controllers Over Security Threat
Progress urges ShareFile admins to shut down servers over "credible" threat

topics.title: Six U-Boot Bootloader Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Firmware security firm Binarly disclosed six new flaws in U-Boot, the small program that starts hardware from home routers and smart cameras to the management chips inside data-center servers; four crash a device, and two let an attacker who slips a malicious image in front of the bootloader run code at boot, opening the door to stealthy, persistent firmware implants.
topics.summary: U-Boot is a widely used open-source bootloader across embedded and IoT devices. Device makers and owners should apply firmware updates as vendors ship them.

sources.title: New U-Boot flaws could enable stealthy firmware attacks
Six New U-Boot Flaws Could Let Malicious Images Crash Devices or Run Code at Boot

topics.title: China and India Spy on Balochistan Police
topics.latest_developments: SentinelOne reported that separate China-linked and India-linked espionage campaigns targeted Pakistan's Balochistan Police—the force covering the insurgency-hit southwestern province—between February 2024 and April 2026, in some cases breaching the exact same systems.
topics.summary: The Balochistan Police oversees a region gripped by a long-running separatist insurgency, drawing intelligence interest from both a rival and a nominal ally. The dual campaigns show a single target absorbing competing state espionage operations.

sources.title: China, India ran separate spying campaigns against same Pakistani police force
China, India-Linked Hackers Both Targeted Same Pakistani Police Force
